notes: orders: each intended order is forced in the kernel by data dependencies or asm volatile clock reads; it holds for this run only where the reorder SASS gate of the binary that measured says PASS (label 'gate' per instantiation). FAIL (E1-E5) and EXCLUDED (E6) instantiations are dropped from every derived figure and listed in 'dropped'; 'gate not run' = no usable PREFIX.reorder_sass.json / reorder_sass.json next to the run; 'not in gate' = the gate lists no such kernel. The gate also fails compared variants whose brackets wait on different scoreboards left outstanding before c0 (pre-bracket waits)

cycles = the bracket c0 .. c1 in SM cycles (body + consume: the closing clock read waits for the consumed results); p10 / p50 / p90 with the sample count n per (variant, params); derived differences are p50 - p50. ns only where a group's brackets span >= 8 %globaltimer ticks, through that group's own SM clock (sum of cycles / sum of timer spans); shorter brackets are cycles only

load_use: L = overlap(0) - chain_only(0) (the load's latency exposed at N = 0, with its dependent address arithmetic, its issue and the consume of its value; serial(0) - chain_only(0) is the cross-check), c = chain_only(0). The overlap chain cannot start before the load is issued: d = the cycles from the seed's data to its first FFMA (the load's address arithmetic, its issue, the clock read that orders the chain after it; 26-27 issue cycles with NVRTC 12.9), which serial's and chain_only's chains do not pay. Model overlap = max(L, 4N + d) + c, serial = L + 4N + c, saving = serial - overlap = min(4N, L - d): L - d is the part of the load's latency a chain can hide. Crossover N* = the knee of overlap(N), least squares a + b * max(N*, N) with b = chain_only's slope (at the top of the measured N it lies beyond the range); model N* = (L - d) / 4. d comes from the knee fit (its intercept - chain_only's) when the knee is inside the range, else from the gate (chain_start_cycles, the binary's issue cycles); both are reported, and a fit that differs from the issue count by more than max(8, d / 4) is an inconsistency (overlap holds a cost the SASS does not explain). overlap2 - overlap = the second independent load's extra cost (both in flight at once)

war: reuse - fresh = the cost of overwriting a register a store has not read yet (stores read their operands late, through the MIO queue). It is a WAR measurement only where the gate decoded a wait on the store's read scoreboard in the reuse build (war_wait true) and none in the fresh build; a reuse build without it is 'not provoked'. The overwrite issues D cycles after the store (war_distance_cycles, the gate's issue count; reuse: the clock read and its LOP3 that order the chain lie between, 12-13 cycles), so the figure is the WAR stall beyond D: an operand read done within D costs 0. reuse_clock - fresh_clock is the same with the first overwrite right after the store where ptxas gave the clock read (or the chain seed's LOP3) the stored register (D = 2-5 with NVRTC 12.9; the gate says per build). fresh - nostore = the store's own cost in the bracket

bar: per rep the late warp (1024 FFMA before the barrier) arrives last. Early warps' c_end - the late warp's c_arrive: pre = release + touch; post = pre when the M register-only FFMA after BAR.SYNC.DEFER_BLOCKING ran during the wait (exposed fraction (post - pre) / 4M near 0), pre + 4M when they waited for the release; post_mem puts a shared load + store before them (expected not to overlap). post's FFMA are ordered after the barrier by a clock read, assumed not to end the deferral (it is not a memory instruction); each warp records when that clock read issued (flags >> 16 = it - c_arrive), and post_clock_during_wait is the fraction of early-warp samples where it issued before the late warp arrived: near 1 the assumption holds; near 0 post cannot tell a clock read that ends the deferral from no deferral at all (post_reading says which). late_sink shift = pre - late_sink of the early warps' c_end - the late warp's c_start (expected 4M). Reps are rebuilt per SM from the arrival stamps (every arrival of a rep precedes its release, a warp's next arrival follows it); incomplete reps are counted and not used. The per-group bracket (groups) is every warp's c_end - c_start, early and late warps pooled; the comparisons use the per-rep stamps

fence: fence cycles = after(M = 0) - chain_only(M = 0): the same clock read, LOP3 and consume STS, plus one fence after one store (the store's drain included). fence_only lacks that scaffolding: fence_only(0) - chain_only(0) + the scaffolding's issue cycles (the gate's after_store_cycles of chain_only(0)) is the cross-check. after - before = what moving the work ahead of the fence saves, against min(fence, W), W = the issue cycles before keeps between its store and its fence (the gate's store_to_fence_cycles: 4M plus the clock read, its LOP3 and the consume STS; else 4M); before's fence also covers that STS, which in after issues behind the fence and nothing waits for. before - chain_only = the fence's exposed part, against max(0, fence - W)

pipe: cycles per FFMA = (c1 - c0) / 1024 per warp (the consume adds ~0.02). k = the time-weighted number of recorded warps on the same SM and sub-partition (%warpid % 4) during that warp's bracket, itself included (unrecorded warm-up brackets are not counted). Expectation max(4 / ILP, p * k), p = 32 / FP32 lanes per sub-partition: 2 on cc 7.x and 8.0, 1 on cc 8.6 / 8.7 / 8.9, 9.0 and later; limit = the term that binds at the median k (the chain's latency, which interleaving ILP chains hides, or the shared FP32 pipe, which it cannot)

stall: slope of cycles = a + b * N over the per-N medians per (OP, MODE). dep_consumed (the chain consumed before c1): slope_cycles_per_link = the issue interval of one dependent link. One warp waits exactly the stall count ptxas encoded before its next instruction, so for the fixed-latency ops the slope reproduces the encoding (encoded_cycles_per_link, the gate's static_cycles_per_link) unless the hardware adds to it (hardware_extra_cycles); the encoding is ptxas's choice, an upper bound on the op's minimum stall, which CuAsmRL finds by lowering stall counts until results go wrong (Tier B's stall-lowering edits test that on the GPU). op_encoded_stall = the stall ptxas put on the op itself (the gate's target_stalls), compared with CuAsmRL's dependency-based A100 table (IADD3, IMAD.IADD, IADD3.X, MOV, IABS, IMAD, FADD, HADD2, IMNMX, SEL, LEA 4; IMAD.WIDE(.U32) 5; the other OPs are not in it): encoded_minus_cuasmrl. A link of IABS (LOP3.LUT + IABS) or IMAD_WIDE (IMAD.WIDE.U32 + the IADD3 of the 64-bit add, its IADD3.X off the chain) holds a helper, so its slope is the link's, not the op's. Variable-latency ops (DADD, DFMA on sm_80 / sm_86) wait on a scoreboard, not on the stall count. dep_unconsumed keeps the slope (each instruction still waits for its predecessor) but the closing clock read does not wait for the last result (intercept about one latency lower); indep's slope is the issue interval of one update (IABS's and IMAD_WIDE's updates issue their helpers too), what a clock-based method without dependencies reports (CuAsmRL measured 2.6 cycles per IADD3 that way); naive_cycles_per_instr = p50 / N at the largest N. An (OP, MODE) with an instantiation the gate EXCLUDED (opcode count != N, or a dependency structure other than the mode's) is dropped from the fits' use and from the table
